rejected.title: Anti-discrimination and equal opportunity
card: Discrimination is treating a worker or applicant worse because of a personal attribute, such as sex, race, age, disability or pregnancy. The person should be judged on their ability to do the job.
Laws ban it in hiring, pay, training, promotion and dismissal. Both Commonwealth and state laws apply.
Equal opportunity means everyone has a fair chance to be hired and to progress. Employers can support it with clear selection criteria based on the skills the job needs.
A business that breaks these laws may face a complaint from the worker, an order to pay compensation and damage to its reputation.
rejected.remember: Hiring, pay and promotion decisions should rest on ability for the job, not on a personal attribute.

a.q: Which decision by an employer would break anti-discrimination law?
opts: Paying a worker less because she has become pregnant
Paying a worker more because of a strong sales record
Promoting the applicant who best meets the criteria
Hiring the applicant with the most relevant skills
a.why: Pregnancy is a personal attribute, and it has nothing to do with how well she does the job. The other decisions rest on results, criteria or skills, so they are based on ability.
a.clue: Look for the decision based on who the person is, not the job.

b.q: Hana runs a bakery in Wagga. Two applicants have equal skills. She rejects Les, who is 58, because she thinks customers prefer younger staff. How is her decision best described?
opts: Discrimination, because age was used instead of ability
Equal opportunity, because both people were interviewed
Equal opportunity, because it pleases her customers
Lawful, because a business may hire whoever it prefers
b.why: Hana rejected Les because of his age when both could do the job, so the decision is discriminatory. Interviewing both does not make it equal opportunity, because the outcome was not based on ability. An owner's wish to please customers or choose freely does not cover a decision based on a banned attribute.
b.clue: Ask what the decision was based on, and whether it relates to ability.

draft.title: Anti-discrimination and equal opportunity
card: Discrimination is treating a worker or job applicant worse because of a personal attribute, such as sex, race, age or disability. Decisions should rest on a person's ability to do the job.
Laws ban discrimination in hiring, pay, training, promotion and dismissal. Both Commonwealth and state laws apply.
Equal opportunity means everyone gets a fair chance to be hired and to move ahead. Clear selection criteria based on the skills the job needs help an employer do this.
A business that breaks these laws may face a complaint from the worker, an order to pay compensation and damage to its reputation.
draft.remember: Hiring, pay and promotion decisions should rest on ability for the job, not on a personal attribute.

a.q: Which decision by an employer would be discrimination?
opts: Refusing a promotion to a worker because she is a woman
Refusing a promotion to a worker who lacks the set skills
Refusing a promotion to a worker who scored lowest in tests
Refusing a promotion to a worker with the weakest results
a.why: Being a woman is a personal attribute and has no link to how well she can do the job. The other three decisions rest on skills, test results or performance, which relate to ability.
a.clue: Which reason has nothing to do with doing the job?

b.q: Hana runs a bakery in Wagga. Two applicants have equal skills. She turns down Les, who is 58, because she thinks customers prefer younger staff. Why is her decision unfair under the law?
opts: She used his age to decide, not his ability for the job
She did not give him a written reason for the decision
She did not advertise the job in the local newspaper
She interviewed only two people before she chose
b.why: Both applicants could do the job, so Hana's choice rested on age, which is a personal attribute. Wanting to please customers does not make age a fair reason. The other options describe steps that are not what makes the decision discriminatory.
b.clue: Both applicants could do the job, so what did she decide on?

a.best: Refusing a promotion to a worker because she is a woman

b.best: She used his age to decide, not his ability for the job
